chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan al-Jammal, who said:
I saw Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in the litter prostrating on a piece of paper, and he did that frequently, indicating with a nod.
ai.seo_question: How did the Imam perform prostration while seated in a litter?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the practical flexibility of Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) in ritual prayer, specifically demonstrating that prostration on a simple piece of paper (*qirtas*) is valid and that frequent, brief prostrations (*bi-ikhtisar*) are a recommended Sunnah. It underscores the Shia emphasis on the purity of the prayer surface and the spiritual discipline of increasing prostration frequency, even in informal settings like a litter. This aligns with the broader jurisprudential principle that any clean, non-edible material can serve as a valid place of prostration.
